terms.comment: Altus is both high and deep, measured from below or from above, so altitūdō is height or depth and the context decides (see height). In altum is out to sea, into the deep.

evidence: Macr. Somn. 1.6.36: longitūdō, lātitūdō, profunditās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Late and technical, for the third dimension; in speech altitūdō serves.

phrases.latin: nātūrā locus jam ante praeceps recentī lāpsū terrae in pedum mīlle admodum altitūdinem abruptus erat
phrases.english: the place, steep by nature already, had broken away in a recent landslide to a depth of nearly a thousand feet
How deep is the water here?

sources: Lewis & Short: altitudo · Lewis & Short: profunditas
